title: Cross-organization full cipher access via unguarded full-access-group query
summary:
# GitHub Security Advisory (vaultwarden)

Split out from the original report, which grouped two primary issues plus a supporting set. The
SSRF and the `post_org_import` gate are tracked separately, see the note at the end.

- **Ecosystem / package:** Rust / self-hosted server - `dani-garcia/vaultwarden`.
- **Affected versions:** 1.27.0 through 1.36.0.
- **Patched versions:** 1.37.0.

## Title
Cross-org full-access authorization gap in vaultwarden

## Severity
**AUTHZ (cross-org full access) - Medium.** Reporter's suggested CVSS v3.1
`AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` (~7.0, but gated on the non-default `org_groups_enabled` +
knowing target UUIDs -> Medium in practice). Assigned as
`AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N` (5.9), matching the reporter's own "Medium in practice"
assessment; `S:U` because both orgs sit under the same authorization component, and `C:L` because
the attacker obtains ciphertext they cannot decrypt without the org key.

## CWEs
CWE-863 / CWE-639 (incorrect authorization / IDOR), CWE-862 (missing authorization).

## Summary
vaultwarden is an internet-exposed, multi-tenant server. An authenticated user who is Admin/Owner of any organization (any user can create one unless `ORG_CREATION_USERS` restricts it) can:

**Cross-organization full cipher access.** `edit_member` / `send_invite`
(`src/api/core/organizations.rs:1606` / `:1162` in 1.36.0) bind body-supplied group UUIDs to a member with no
`Group::find_by_uuid_and_org` check (unlike the collections loop and `put_group_members`), planting a
cross-org `groups_users` row. Then `Group::is_in_full_access_group` (`src/db/models/group.rs:261`) - the
query behind `Cipher::get_access_restrictions` - lacks the `groups.organizations_uuid ==
users_organizations.org_uuid` guard its sibling `get_orgs_by_user_with_full_access` (`group.rs:243`) has,
so that stray row grants full read/write/manage on a foreign org's ciphers to a non-member. Requires
`org_groups_enabled=true` (non-default) and knowing target group + cipher UUIDs (no enumeration).

## Proof of concept
Source-only, offline, provided privately:
- `poc/poc_authz_cross_org_full_access.py` - SQLite repro of the two Diesel queries: the unguarded
`is_in_full_access_group` grants a non-member cross-org full access, the guarded sibling denies it on
identical data. (`RESULT_authz_cross_org.txt`)

## Impact
An authenticated user who is Admin/Owner of any organization (with the groups feature enabled) can gain full read/write/manage on specific
ciphers of an organization they are not a member of. Vault contents remain client-side encrypted
throughout.

## Remediation
Add the org-match join guard to `Group::is_in_full_access_group` (matching
`get_orgs_by_user_with_full_access`) and validate group-org in `edit_member`/`send_invite`.

Both were applied in 1.37.0.

## Split-out issues
The original report also covered, and the reporter is credited as a finder on both:
- Unauthenticated favicon SSRF bypassing the non-global-IP filter -> GHSA-hw4g-2v3f-74x5
- Read-only collection member injecting ciphers via `post_org_import` -> GHSA-f3qw-qg77-hmm4
